name: Heroic Labs

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Nakama on Heroic Cloud (production)
plans.note: Calculator: $400 x Nakama CPUs + $200 x database CPUs per month (default 1+1 = $600). Satori on Heroic Cloud starts from $600/month (event-based ingestion pricing, bespoke above). Development instances (burstable CPU, micro DB, CI) exist but their price is not published. Billing: usage metered daily at the day's highest CPU count, prorated, invoiced monthly via Stripe; deployments cannot be paused, charges stop the day after deletion. Support: Studio Basic $2,000, Studio Standard $6,000, Studio Premium contact (optional, on top).

plans.name: Satori on Heroic Cloud
plans.note: LiveOps product, event-based ingestion pricing, 'starts from' $600/month; bespoke above.

caveats: Public managed multiplayer app backend supporting developer server modules. Rendered default Nakama calculator $600/mo includes database and managed platform; no 4/8-only price guaranteed. Support $2000/$6000 optional, not mandatory compute plans. Dedicated/HA/BYOC changes price.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
snapshot_auto.note: No stop/sleep lifecycle to snapshot on. Separate: automatic daily differential database backups on a rolling 7-day window (restore via Heroic Labs support), which are scheduled backups, not snapshot_auto.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Use Data Export to download a complete PostgreSQL snapshot of your deployment's database for backup, analysis, migration, or any other reason.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Only an on-demand PostgreSQL database export (download, pg_restore yourself); no machine/server snapshot and no booting new deployments from a snapshot. Managed Nakama game-backend PaaS, not a VM/sandbox.

guest_firewall.note: No shell/root on nodes: customer code is Nakama runtime modules (Go/TypeScript-JS/Lua) compiled by Builders into container images run by the platform; JS runs in Nakama's sandboxed JSVM.

secret_proxy.quote: Runtime variables are environment variables injected into your Nakama processes.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are runtime secret variables (env) or secret configurations merged into Nakama config at startup; secret flag only limits who can read the value back in the dashboard.

isolation.quote: Dedicated Resources: Your instance is exclusively assigned to you with dedicated hardware resources.
isolation.note: Managed Nakama/Satori PaaS; production deployments run on dedicated hardware/VMs per title rather than a shared multi-tenant kernel, but customers never see or choose a hypervisor/isolation tech directly.

image_oci.quote: A builder connects to your Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket), compiles your server code against a specific Nakama version, and produces a container image that you deploy to one or more Nakama instances.
image_oci.note: You supply source code (Go/TypeScript-JS/Lua server modules) via Git; Heroic Cloud's own Builder compiles the container image. There is no way to start a deployment from your own arbitrary Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: A Nakama deployment is your complete game backend. When you create one, Heroic Cloud provisions the entire dedicated stack. You don't configure individual components or manage the underlying infrastructure.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No shell/root access to run additional containers inside a deployment; the only workload is the Nakama process running your compiled server modules.

nested_virt.quote: You don't configure individual components or manage the underlying infrastructure. Everything below is set up, maintained, and operated by Heroic Cloud.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Fully managed game-backend PaaS; no /dev/kvm or guest-level machine access is exposed.

desktop.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. It is a server-side game backend, not a desktop/VM product.

browser.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed browser is part of Nakama/Satori/Hiro.

computer_use.quote: Real-time multiplayer, matchmaking, leaderboards, tournaments, social features (friends, groups, chat), player profiles, virtual wallets, and server-side scripting in Go, TypeScript, and Lua.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Game backend PaaS; no screenshot/click desktop-driving API.

anti_bot.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Game backend/LiveOps platform, not a browser-automation/anti-detection product.

captcha_solving.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: You don't configure individual components or manage the underlying infrastructure. Everything below is set up, maintained, and operated by Heroic Cloud.
ssh.note: Access is via the dashboard/API and the Nakama Console; there is no SSH to underlying nodes.

snapshot.quote: Use Data Export to download a complete PostgreSQL snapshot of your deployment's database for backup, analysis, migration, or any other reason.
snapshot.note: Only an on-demand database (PostgreSQL) export exists; there is no machine/server snapshot or ability to boot a new deployment from a snapshot.

fork.quote: Instance name must be unique and becomes part of your DNS hostname... Once set, the instance name can't be changed.
fork.note: No documented ability to clone a running deployment into a new one; new deployments are created and configured from scratch (or a database export can be restored by support).

fork_running.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
fork_running.note: No fork capability exists at all (see fork).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Use Data Export to download a complete PostgreSQL snapshot of your deployment's database for backup, analysis, migration, or any other reason.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork feature exists; only a database export/restore mechanism, which does not carry over running process/memory state.

wake_on_request.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
wake_on_request.note: Deployments run continuously; there is no sleep/wake-on-request lifecycle.

persistent_disk.quote: Own Your Data: Your application data belongs to you and is stored separately to all other users in our cloud. Easily export backups for your own analysis.
persistent_disk.note: Nakama's PostgreSQL database persists across restarts/deploys (rolling updates), backed by automated backups.

volume_attach.quote: The database scales independently from the Nakama nodes. This lets you size compute and storage separately based on your workload.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Storage is the managed Nakama/Satori database, not an attachable generic block volume.

volume_shared.quote: The database scales independently from the Nakama nodes.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No generic multi-mount volume concept; all Nakama nodes share the one managed database, not a filesystem volume.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
auto_stop_idle.note: Deployments run continuously and are billed/metered regardless of idle activity until deleted.

live_resize.quote: When you apply a tier change, Nakama performs a rolling reboot: each pod restarts one at a time... With a single node, expect brief downtime during the restart.
live_resize.note: Changing CPU/RAM tier requires a rolling reboot of nodes (no downtime only if 2+ nodes already provisioned); it is not a live, in-place resize with zero restart.

agent_harnesses.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No coding-agent templates; server runtimes are Go/TypeScript-JS/Lua game logic modules.

harness_api.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Satori: LiveOps platform for operating and optimizing live games with measurable, data-driven workflows.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Satori is a LiveOps/analytics product, not a browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
mcp_server.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No MCP server for controlling sandboxes/deployments found in docs.

lang_python.quote: Nakama supports three runtimes for custom game server logic: Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Lua.
lang_python.note: Python is not one of the supported server-module runtimes.

lang_node.quote: TypeScript / JavaScript ... The Heroic Cloud builder looks for a pre-bundled JavaScript (.js) file ... TypeScript/JavaScript runs inside a sandboxed virtual machine (JSVM).
lang_node.note: JS/TS server modules are a first-class supported runtime, executed by Nakama's JSVM (not a general Node.js host, but Node/JS logic is supported out of the box).

public_ipv4.quote: Each deployment gets a unique hostname in the format {instance-name}.{zone}.heroiclabs.com on port 443 (TLS encrypted).
public_ipv4.note: Deployments are reached via a managed hostname behind a load balancer; no per-deployment public IPv4 address is documented or exposed.

inbound_https.quote: Each deployment gets a unique hostname in the format {instance-name}.{zone}.heroiclabs.com on port 443 (TLS encrypted).

ingress_rules.quote: Heroic Cloud's access control system handles this through three concepts: principals (teams, users, and service users)... permission layers... conflict resolution.
ingress_rules.note: Access control governs dashboard/API permissions for users, not network-level control (IP allowlists/security groups) over who can reach the exposed game-client hostname/port.

egress_allowlist.quote: Runtime variables are environment variables injected into your Nakama processes... Use runtime variables for values your own code needs: feature flags, endpoints for third-party services.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented; server modules can call third-party endpoints freely via runtime configuration.

egress_http_rules.quote: Runtime variables are environment variables injected into your Nakama processes.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rules are documented.

gpu.quote: Production Nakama instances scale across a range of tiers, from Nano (1 CPU / 3.75 GB RAM) up to 7XLarge (120 CPU / 360 GB RAM).
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only CPU/RAM tiers are offered for Nakama/database nodes; no GPU tier.

windows.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Managed Linux-based game-server backend; no customer-facing Windows machines.

macos.quote: Heroic Labs builds the Heroic Game Stack — open-source and managed backend infrastructure for game studios and publishers.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

hipaa.quote: Heroic Cloud is a managed or private cloud built for scaling the Heroic Game stack for the biggest games.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A gaming backend/LiveOps platform; no HIPAA/BAA offering found in docs.

eu_data_residency.quote: Multi-Region Deployment: Heroic Cloud is available on GCP or AWS in North America, Europe and Asia. More regions on request.
eu_data_residency.note: European GCP/AWS zones can be chosen at deployment creation, and the deployment zone/region can't be changed later, keeping data in that region.

max_session_h.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
max_session_h.note: A deployment runs indefinitely (billed continuously) until explicitly deleted; there is no maximum session/runtime limit.

egress_ip_type.quote: Every production type deployment gets its own DNS, load balancer, Nakama server nodes, and PostgreSQL database, all running on hardware reserved for your title.
egress_ip_type.note: Heroic Cloud runs Nakama/Satori deployments on GCP and AWS infrastructure (per docs, 'Heroic Cloud runs on both GCP and AWS'); outbound traffic from these managed backend servers uses standard cloud-provider datacenter IPs. No residential/mobile IP product is offered — this is a managed multiplayer game-backend PaaS, not a proxy/scraping product.

static_egress_ip.quote: The database replica and profiling add-ons extend your production deployment with capabilities beyond the standard offering
static_egress_ip.note: No add-on, enterprise feature, or docs page mentions a fixed/static outbound IP for deployments. VPC peering (Private Cloud) covers private connectivity, not a published static egress IP. Not offered: outside the product's scope as documented.

arm64.quote: How to setup and run Nakama binary and its prerequisites on any X86_64 Linux distribution.
arm64.note: Nakama binary/docs reference X86_64 Linux; Heroic Cloud gives no customer-facing choice of CPU architecture (managed PaaS, not an IaaS VM product) and no ARM/Graviton/Apple-silicon offering is documented anywhere in the product or pricing pages. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

pause_resume.quote: Deployments can't be paused, stopped, or temporarily disabled. A deployment is either provisioned or it isn't.
pause_resume.note: Official docs explicitly state deployments cannot be paused/stopped; matches the plan note that deployments cannot be paused and billing continues until deletion.

cpu_class.quote: Dedicated Resources: Your instance is exclusively assigned to you with dedicated hardware resources.
cpu_class.note: Production Nakama/Satori deployments run on hardware reserved exclusively for the title (per-tier vCPU counts, e.g. Nano 1 CPU up to 7XLarge 120 CPU per docs/scaling page), with no CPU sharing/oversubscription across customers. Development instances are noted elsewhere to use burstable CPU, but their published baseline % is not documented, so only the production 'native' mode is scored here.

usage_api.quote: Fetch billing for a period, or a single invoice by ID... Deployment logs and metrics aren't available through this API.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; Heroic Cloud has a billing API (GetBilling) that returns account-level invoices for a period, not granular per-deployment usage. The metric exporting add-on provides application performance metrics (CPU%, memory%, requests/sec) aggregated across all nodes in a deployment, but not billable usage (vCPU-seconds, GB-seconds, CPU allocation hours). Billable usage is metered daily by deployment tier/type for billing invoices, but this granular usage data is not exposed programmatically per deployment or with deployment tags/labels.
